radio.description: The radio hardware (changes need a restart).

hpsdr.description: HPSDR Protocol 1 server (changes need a restart).

limits.description: Sessions and channel sharing (apply at once).

station.description: The station, as reported with spots (apply at once).

syslog.description:
The skimmers' log (spots, band and upload events) to a syslog
receiver (apply at once).

mqtt.description: The same to an MQTT broker (apply at once).

markers.description: Frequency labels and the band ribbon (apply at once).

dxspots.description:
Live DX spots from a Spothole server, as labels on the spectrum
(apply at once).

update.description:
Updates of the OS (web888-ng-os) from the admin page: the check for
a new release and its install (apply at once).

kiwi.description:
KiwiSDR protocol clients: kiwirecorder, SuperSDR, ... (apply at
once; `doc/m5-kiwi.md`).

info.description: The receiver's info page for listeners (apply at once).

propagation.description: HF propagation forecasts for listeners (apply at once).

timecode.description:
LF time-code stations watched on the receiver (changes need a
restart).

timesync.description:
The system clock fed from the receiver's own time sources (the
time-code stations) through chrony (changes need a restart).

bitstream.description:
zynqsdr: `auto` (the image's channelizer for the band if it has
one, else as `standard`), `channelizer`, `standard` (the image's or
the stock bitstream with the hardware's DDCs, 12 RX on HF), a path,
or `none` (already loaded).

band.description:
zynqsdr: `hf`, or `vhf`: the VHF RF path, the Si5351 ADC clock at
98.304 MHz, 98.304..147.456 MHz tunable (undersampled).

si5351_adc.description: EXPERIMENTAL (test unit only): reprogram the Si5351 ADC clock (Hz).

bins.description:
RX channels from a channelizer's bins (`doc/m6-channelizer.md`):
how many. Backend iq: runs its software bank; zynqsdr: needs the
channelizer bitstream (`bitstream = "/usr/share/web888/websdr_pfb.bit"`)
and uses 32 when not set. The waterfall stays the backend's.

zoom_engine.description:
Bins mode: zoomed waterfalls from the source's zoom engine when it
has one (`hw/docs/channelizer.md` §3.9), instead of FFTs here.

atten_db.description:
zynqsdr: the RF attenuator before the ADC, 0 (off) to 31.5 dB in
0.5 dB steps, for every listener at once: against ADC overloads
from strong signals. Applies at once (no restart); an HPSDR client
may change it while it runs.

freq_offset_hz.description:
A converter in front of the receiver (Hz): every frequency shown to
web listeners and every skimmer spot (PSKReporter, WSPRnet, MQTT,
syslog, the map) is the receiver's own plus this, e.g. 116000000
for a 2 m converter with its 144 MHz at 28 MHz. 0: none. Skimmer
dials and the label lists stay the receiver's own; the frequency
labels and the band ribbon are hidden while it is set. Kiwi and
HPSDR clients see the receiver's own frequencies.

adc_dither.description:
zynqsdr: the ADC's dither (LTC2208 DITH): spreads the ADC's
spurs into the noise, at a little noise. Applies at once.

iq.description: Backend iq: the wideband IQ input.

oneOf.description: Wideband IQ from an SDR or a recording, channelized like the FPGA.

Band.description: The band the antenna input is used for (zynqsdr backend).

oneOf.description: 0..61.44 MHz at the 122.88 MHz ADC clock (the HF path).

98.304..147.456 MHz (airband, 2 m) by undersampling at a 98.304
MHz ADC clock (the VHF path; the stock airband profile 0).

tones.description: Tones at the antenna: [frequency Hz, level dBFS].

noise.description: Add the typical ADC noise floor.

bandwidth.description: Device analog bandwidth (Hz, 0 = the driver's choice).

loop.description: Start a file again at its end.

board.description: Board id reported to clients (1 = Hermes, 5 = Orion, 6 = Hermes-Lite).

listen.description: HTTPS and plain HTTP on one port.

state_dir.description: Where web888d keeps state (the self-signed certificate).

default_freq.description: Initial dial frequency (Hz; default 7.066 MHz if in range).

wf_budget.description:
Most FFTs averaged per waterfall line (CPU budget; default 30, 6 on
32-bit ARM, where an FFT costs ~100x more: `doc/m3-multi-user.md` §4).

metrics_allow.description:
Clients (addresses or networks, e.g. "192.168.1.0/24") allowed to
read `/metrics`; others get 403. Empty: nobody.

trusted_proxies.description:
Reverse proxies (addresses or networks, e.g. "10.0.0.5",
"192.168.0.0/16") whose X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are
believed: for requests from them, the client is the rightmost
forwarded address that isn't a trusted proxy itself.

allowed_origins.description:
Other web sites whose pages may open listening sessions (`/ws`)
from their visitors' browsers, as origins ("https://example.org");
"*": any site. Pages served from this receiver's own address
always may, and programs (which send no Origin) aren't affected.

oneOf.description: Plain HTTP only (behind a TLS-terminating proxy).

per_ip.description: Sessions per client address (0 = no limit).

trusted.description:
Addresses or networks (e.g. "192.0.2.7", "10.0.0.0/8") whose
sessions `per_ip` doesn't limit: your own network, test machines.

session_minutes.description:
Web session time limit, minutes (0 = none). Admins aren't
limited; users get a notice a minute before, and reconnect by hand.

idle_minutes.description:
Idle limit, minutes without input (tuning, mode, waterfall or
audio changes; 0 = none). As `session_minutes` otherwise.

preempt.description: Higher classes may take channels from lower ones.

hpsdr_channels.description: Most RX channels HPSDR clients may hold.

share_default.description:
Show users' frequencies to others and allow listen-along, unless
the user opts out.

skimmers_yield.description:
Skimmers give their channels to users when none is free, and get
one again when a channel frees.

daily_minutes.description:
Listening time per client address and UTC day, minutes (0 = no
limit): once used up, new sessions are refused and a running one
ends (a minute's notice), until 00:00 UTC. Admins and `trusted`
addresses aren't limited.

blocked.description:
Addresses or networks refused (web and Kiwi clients), e.g.
"192.0.2.7" or "198.51.100.0/24"; the admin page's Ban adds here.
Admins still get in.

open_channels.description:
With a listener password: how many receivers visitors without it
may use at once (they queue for one beyond that; with the password
any). 0: the password is needed to listen at all.

callsign.description: Callsign spots are reported under (needed for uploads).

locator.description:
Maidenhead locator, 4 or 6 characters (needed for uploads; with
gpsd, used until there is a fix).

gpsd.description:
gpsd to take the locator from, `host` or `host:port` (port 2947),
e.g. `127.0.0.1`; empty: off.

hours.description: UTC hours to run, e.g. "18-06" or "0-24"; empty = always.

pskreporter.description:
Upload spots to PSKReporter (needs [station] callsign and locator;
live signals only).

wsprnet.description:
Upload WSPR spots to WSPRnet (needs [station] callsign and locator;
live signals only).

server.description:
The receiver, `host` or `host:port` (port 514; IPv6 in brackets,
`[2001:db8::1]:514`); empty: off.

modes.description: Spots of these modes only; empty: all.

hostname.description: The host name in messages; empty: the system's.

oneOf.description: The older BSD format, RFC 3164 (`<134>Oct 24 21:11:45 host web888d: ...`).

LogEvent.description: What the skimmers log, for choosing what goes to syslog and MQTT.

oneOf.description:
Bands starting and stopping, their problems, and the station's
locator from gpsd.
What the uploaders (PSKReporter, WSPRnet) did, and their errors.
ADC overloads: when, how long, and the signal that caused them.

server.description:
The broker, `host` or `host:port` (port 1883; IPv6 in brackets);
empty: off.

topic.description:
Topics start with this; empty: `web888/<host name>`. Spots go to
`<topic>/spot/<MODE>`, events to `<topic>/band` and
`<topic>/upload`, and `<topic>/status` is `online` (retained;
`offline` as the broker's last will).

modes.description: Spots of these modes only; empty: all.

region.description:
IARU region (1-3) of the band ribbon and the amateur frequencies,
until a listener picks another.

file.description:
The station's own labels (CSV; the admin pages upload and download
it). A relative path is next to this configuration file.

DxSpots.description:
Live DX spots: web888d follows a Spothole server's spot stream
(<https://spothole.app>, an aggregator of DX clusters and outdoor
activity programmes) and shows the spots in the receiver's range as
labels on the spectrum.

enabled.description: Follow the spots (an HTTPS connection to `server`).

sources.description:
Spothole's sources to take: "Cluster" (DX clusters), and e.g.
"POTA", "SOTA", "WWFF", "GMA", "HEMA" (its /options lists them).

de_continents.description:
Only spots by spotters on these continents (EU, NA, SA, AS, AF, OC,
AN); empty: all.

max_age_minutes.description: A spot is shown this long (minutes; Spothole keeps them an hour).

ca_file.description:
CA certificates (PEM) to check the server with; empty: the
system's, else the built-in roots of Let's Encrypt.

Update.description:
OS updates: on the web888-ng-os image (with RAUC), the admin page shows
whether a newer release is out and installs it into the other root
slot (the receiver keeps running; a reboot starts the new system, and
a system that doesn't come up falls back to the old one).

enabled.description:
Look for new releases and allow installing them (only where RAUC
is installed: the OS image).

releases.description: The releases (the GitHub API's list of a repository's releases).

check_hours.description:
Look by itself every this many hours (0: only from the admin
page). Nothing is installed without the admin.

prereleases.description: Releases marked as pre-releases count too.

ca_file.description:
CA certificates (PEM) to check the server with; empty: the
system's.

enabled.description:
Accept Kiwi protocol connections (`/<n>/SND`, `/<n>/W/F`) and
answer `/status`.

name.description:
The receiver's name, as clients and `/status` show it (empty:
"web888d" and the callsign).

smeter_offset_db.description:
dBm = dBFS + this, for the S-meter and the waterfall levels Kiwi
clients get (web888d measures dBFS; calibrate with a known signal).

Info.description:
What the receiver's info page tells listeners, beside the name and
location (`[kiwi] name`, `location`), the station's callsign, locator
and antenna (`[station]`), and a photo uploaded from the admin page.

description.description:
A few words about the receiver: the antenna's setup, the noise,
what it is meant for (plain text; blank lines start paragraphs).

contact.description:
How to reach the owner (shown as written; an address here is public).
Also given as the contact for privacy questions.

privacy.description:
More for the info page's Privacy section, after what web888d says
itself (e.g. who runs the receiver, a proxy in front of it and its
logs).

reception_notice.description:
Tell listeners that what isn't meant for the public may be heard
but not passed on or used.

Propagation.description:
HF propagation forecasts (`doc/m2-web-ui.md` §13): VOACAP from a few
regions to the receiver (at `[station] locator`), per UTC hour and
band, for the month. Works with no network: the sunspot number is
`ssn`, else NOAA's prediction when it can be fetched (kept on disk),
else a table built into the server.

engine.description:
"voacap": the month's median; "truecast": the same model at the
day's index (the month's sunspot number with a fitted correction
for the day of the year).

ssn.description: A fixed smoothed sunspot number, instead of NOAA's or the built-in.

fetch.description:
Fetch NOAA's predicted sunspot numbers (daily) and the planetary
K index (every 30 minutes). Off: no connections are made.

ssn_url.description: Where they come from (NOAA SWPC's JSON, or a copy of it).

ca_file.description:
CA certificates (PEM) to check the server with; empty: the
system's.

power_w.description: The transmitter's power (W), with isotropic antennas at both ends.

noise_dbw.description:
Man-made noise at the receiver, at 3 MHz (dBW in 1 Hz): -136
industrial, -145 residential, -150 rural, -153 remote.

targets.description: The regions, as signals from there to the receiver.

Timecode.description:
LF time-code stations decoded on the receiver, from one channelizer
bin (`doc/api.md` §8.5): each minute's carrier level, keying, decode,
lateness against the receiver's clock and the ADC clock's error
measured on the carrier, as metrics and a log. Needs the channelizer's
bins.

centre_hz.description:
The bin nearest this frequency (Hz) is watched for the stations
whose carrier is within 21 kHz of its centre; any other station in
the bin nearest its carrier (a bin more each: its own floor).

region.description:
Which stations, when `stations` is empty: "auto" those within
reach of the receiver (`[station] locator`), or a region's:
"europe" (DCF77, MSF, RBU, TDF, DCF39, HGA22, DCF49),
"north-america" (WWVB), "east-asia" (JJY), or "all". Each station
costs CPU (~0.5-1 % of a core): only what can be received.

stations.description:
The stations, by name (overrides `region`): DCF77, MSF, RBU,
TDF (162 kHz), WWVB, JJY (40 and 60 kHz: whichever is in a bin
watched), and EFR's teleswitch stations DCF39 (139 kHz), HGA22
(135.6 kHz), DCF49 (129.1 kHz): a time telegram every 10 s.

log.description:
A line per station and minute (JSON) to `timecode.log` in the
state directory (kept under 10 MB, the older half in
`timecode.log.1`).

Timesync.description:
The receiver's time sources (today the `[timecode]` stations) as a
reference clock for chrony (`doc/api.md` §8.5): each minute one
sample, the sources' offsets of the system clock combined by their
scatter, to chrony's SOCK socket (`refclock SOCK PATH` in
chrony.conf; the OS image has it). chrony weighs it against its NTP
servers and keeps the clock with it when they are gone.

chrony_socket.description:
chrony's socket (empty: no samples to chrony; the sources are
still measured and shown).

trim_ms.description:
Per source (station name, e.g. `RBU`), milliseconds added to its
offsets: a calibration beyond the built-in one (the path from the
transmitter by `[station] locator`, the decoder's own delay).
